subject.title: [Bug]: cloud-worker reconcile conflict is unrecoverable: stuck turn claim, blocked reclaim, restart destroys pending result

question: When a cloud-worker workspace conflict is genuine rather than an excluded derived artifact, should the Gateway preserve the remote result and worker for explicit operator retry across restart, and what local-versus-remote authority must that retry enforce?
rationale: The remaining behavior spans session ownership, managed-worktree conflict policy, operator UX, and restart cleanup; code inspection alone cannot choose the acceptable data-authority and recovery semantics.

options.title: Preserve and recover pending work
options.body: Keep the worker and its pending remote result through conflicts and restart, release the turn claim promptly, and provide an explicit retry/resolve flow that validates local authority before applying changes.

options.title: Fail closed with explicit abandonment
options.body: Treat genuine divergence as terminal, but document that policy and provide a visible operator action that snapshots or exports the remote result before cleanup.

recommendation.title: Preserve and recover pending work
recommendation.body: Keep the worker and its pending remote result through conflicts and restart, release the turn claim promptly, and provide an explicit retry/resolve flow that validates local authority before applying changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked merged and open cloud-worker lifecycle work provide the strongest available ownership signal for the required recovery-contract decision.
